claims.text: Microsoft's Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because, despite claims of encryption, security researchers demonstrated that its screenshots were stored unencrypted (in plaintext) within a local SQLite database [Source: ev-1].
This allowed any process running as the user to access sensitive content captured by default, including passwords and private messages [Source: ev-1].

The incident was announced on May 20, 2024, at the Copilot+ PC launch, leading to investigations by regulatory bodies such as the Irish Data Protection Commission and the Washington State Attorney General [Source: ev-1].
Additionally, accessing the timeline now requires Windows Hello authentication and presence detection, while incognito and DRM content are excluded from capture [Source: ev-1].
This revised version reached general availability in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
